added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken
added_failures_source: the reviewed run's own manifest read through annotate_review_of_run: it names no baseline_suite and no after_suite field, so the count is unmeasured rather than zero, and the run's live pointer carries suite_command null so the two armed-only fields were correctly omitted. Controls on this reader: a synthetic base/head pair differing by one FAILED id returns count 1 with that id, and the manifest of r-20260930T170220223668-repair-of-hook-tests-pin-their-harness-a7219b131d65, which carries both fields, returns a measured 0 with base log revision 1f88db44c, so the unmeasured reading is the manifest's shape and not a silent reader (derivation.log in this review's run directory).

findings.text: the after window's cross-task figure is asserted against the verdict field the scanner derives from that same count at docs/research/scripts/scan_local_session_carryover.py:954, so the assertion cannot fail for any census the scanner emits and a classification regression would only redden it if the census were regenerated — the only independent guard is the positive-control test above it.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against bcaf26dcf; f2ba004b8 lands the scanner and the census it regenerates, 373754eaf lands the gate, the fragment and the figure, and dc42bc5d5 repoints the fragment at the control logs kept in the run directory, and no production module is touched by the three.
item_verdicts.done_when: the measure names a scanner, a census, a gate pair, a size bound, a time bound, a fragment and a figure, and each exists at dc42bc5d5 — docs/research/data/local-session-carryover.json is 256,957 bytes against the 300,000-byte bound, its wall_seconds is 28.6 against the 1200-second bound, and the gate re-run at that revision reads 9 passed EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to measure whether a local-lane dispatch still carries another task's session into its first turn since reuse was keyed to the run's own task, and to complete the local half of the census whose codex half is docs/research/data/codex-resume-burn-after.json; docs/research/data/local-session-carryover.json answers it over both windows with that file's own classes, window rule and summary fields.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names three commits, the gate command with absolute paths and its result, the run directory's control logs and the deleted scratch, and states its landing in one line — it records the gate under the tests field rather than the two arms, which the run's own live pointer confirms is correct for it since suite_command is null and the arms are armed-only.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared scope is docs/research/scripts/scan_local_session_carryover.py, docs/research/data/local-session-carryover.json, tests/test_local_session_carryover.py, docs/evidence/fragments/a-review-dies-where-nobody-is-looking/local-session-carryover.html and the figure directory; git diff bcaf26dcf..dc42bc5d5 changes six files and every one of them is inside that set.

justifications.durability: the control test is a real guard — the declared negative control reddens it with 1 failed EXIT=1 and the unmutated scratch tree ran green first at 6 passed, so the red is the mutation — but tests/test_local_session_carryover.py:98 compares the after window's cross-task count with data["cross_task_resumes_verdict"], which docs/research/scripts/scan_local_session_carryover.py:954 computes from that same count, so that assertion holds for every census the scanner can emit.
justifications.evidence: the result is recorded rather than claimed — gate.log:1 names revision dc42bc5d5 and its last line reads EXIT=0, I re-ran both named gate files at that revision for 9 passed EXIT=0 in 0.77 s, and ruff check and ruff format --check over the three changed Python files report nothing — deducting two because the fragment's gate section quotes the scan command without its --stdout-summary flag where scan.log holds the literal command, and because the census figures are asserted against the committed file rather than re-derived in the gate.
justifications.fit: the scanner and the plot script follow the sibling census and figure scripts (docs/research/scripts/scan_local_lane_deaths.py and docs/figures/a-review-dies-where-nobody-is-looking/plot_local_lane_deaths.py carry the same file-local palette constants and class vocabulary) and the commits carry conventional subjects with bodies and no plan label or attribution, deducting one because the palette is duplicated a further time rather than shared.
justifications.goal_fidelity: docs/research/data/local-session-carryover.json reports 270 cross-task resumes over 1,828 dispatches before the boundary and zero over 1,439 after it, and I re-derived that zero from a second instrument — the run store's own session column gives 1,371 after-window local rows in 1,367 distinct sessions with no shared id, against 102 shared session ids before the boundary — deducting one because a resumed attempt's own first turn is not read, as docs/evidence/fragments/a-review-dies-where-nobody-is-looking/local-session-carryover.html:149 states.
justifications.scope_discipline: all six changed paths in git diff bcaf26dcf..dc42bc5d5 sit inside the declared write paths, the fragment and the figure are the two artefacts the done-when names, no plan file, shared index or sprint state is touched, and the scratch /tmp/local-session-carryover is absent exactly as the manifest claims.
